newsitem.title: USA: USDA ups US FY97 cotton, soybean export forecasts.
newsitem.headline: USDA ups US FY97 cotton, soybean export forecasts.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department on Monday boosted its forecast for soybean and cotton exports in the 1997 fiscal year, citing heavy shipments to China, the European Union and Mexico.

USDA said its forecast for soybean exports was raised by 700,000 tonnes and $700 million from December's projection to 24.4 million tonnes valued at $7.1 billion. The soybean meal forecast was raised by 300,000 tonnes and $200 million to six million tonnes valued at $1.5 billion.
The forecast for cotton was raised 100,000 tonnes and $500 million from the last estimate to 1.5 million tonnes valued at $2.6 billion.
Forecasts for wheat and coarse grain exports were both shaved about 1.0 million tonnes, largely due to stiff competition from abroad.
The value of U.S. beef and pork exports was lowered $200 million from the December estimate to $4.7 billion but the volume forecast was left unchanged.

The export forecast for poultry and products remained at a record $3.0 billion despite a slight upward revision in poultry meat export volume to 2.7 million tonnes. USDA said somewhat lower prices for leg quarters are now expected.

Earlier, in a speech at USDA's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman announced the department had revised up its forecast for total fiscal 1997 agricultural exports by $1.0 billion to $56.5 billion.
